gen-fs-telma-fs-karma: Karma reads like a classic serif, trustworthy and unhurried, with terminals that stop well short of the stem and capitals barely taller than the lowercase. Telma's flowing script handwriting sits above it, graceful and good for a handful of lines.
gen-fs-telma-fs-paquito: Paquito brings a confident, approachable text serif with capitals sitting close to the lowercase height, while Telma's flowing script stays gentle above it. It stays friendly through a longer passage, and Telma is best kept to a handful of lines.
gen-fs-telma-montserrat: Telma writes its lowercase a with a wide mouth and a high mean line, graceful and understated from the first word. Montserrat is a geometric sans with big open counters, and it glides underneath while Telma stays comfortable in small doses.
gen-fs-trench-slab-archivo: Heavy, industrial, built big. Trench Slab does the shouting with its outsized lowercase, while Archivo handles the talking, its curves opening outward and its tall x-height keeping a sans editorial and approachable.
gen-fs-trench-slab-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Be Vietnam Pro takes the body, with strokes like bent steel rod and a mean line set high, clean and neutral. And Trench Slab, industrial and oversized in the lowercase, gives the pair its loudest quality.
gen-fs-trench-slab-rubik: Rubik reads soft and clear, its round open letters holding up even at small sizes. Rubik's big lowercase beside capitals is the pair's strongest quality, and it gives Trench Slab's industrial slabs room to stand out.
gen-fs-zina-clash-grotesk: Zina is refined and striking, with fat downstrokes, threadlike upstrokes and wide-set spacing that is better for brief copy. And Clash Grotesk sits beneath it in a clean sans-serif with no swelling in the bowls, so the page stays approachable.
gen-fs-zina-fs-literata: Fat stems, hairline strokes, pure drama. Zina's closed, striking letters stand against Literata's wide-mouthed curves, and that open, bookish serif softness is what makes the pair feel so sophisticated.
gen-fs-zina-fs-roundo: Refined and striking, Zina cuts its letters from fat downstrokes and threadlike upstrokes. Roundo does the opposite job, a geometric sans-serif with unclogged small counters, made for short stretches of reading.
gen-fs-zina-fs-rowan: Sharp-edged and dramatic, Zina snaps from thick to hairline within each letter. Rowan's strongest quality is the gradual, friendly weight change in its open serif curves, though it is not meant for long paragraphs.
